newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS BEAT LIGHTNING FOR FIRST WIN AT TAMPA BAY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS BEAT LIGHTNING FOR FIRST WIN AT TAMPA BAY.

text.p: Martin Rucinsky scored twice and Jocelyn Thibault made 35 saves as the Montreal Canadiens posted their first-ever victory at Tampa Bay with a 4-1 triumph over the Lightning on Thursday.
Brian Savage and Mark Recchi also scored for Montreal, which improved to 1-6-2 all-time at Tampa Bay.
Shayne Corson, Vincent Damphousse and Valeri Bure added two assists apiece for Montreal.

At Florida, red-hot John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 37 shots and Radek Dvorak and Robert Svehla scored first-period goals, leading the Florida Panthers to their fourth straight win, 3-1 over the Boston Bruins.
Jody Hull also scored and Ray Sheppard had two assists for Florida, which has won four straight games.
"It was not a pretty third period, not a pretty win, but they don't all have to be pretty," Florida defenceman Gord Murphy said.

In Ottawa, the line of Geoff Courtnall, Pierre Turgeon and Brett Hull combined for three goals and six assists to lead the surging St. Louis Blues to their sixth win in their last seven games, 5-2 over the Ottawa Senators.
Turgeon led the way with a goal and three assists for St. Louis, which climbed over Detroit into second-place in the Central Division with 54 points.
In Vancouver, Jyrki Lumme scored on a backhander 90 seconds into overtime to lift the Vancouver Canucks to a 2-1 victory over the New York Islanders.
From the opening faceoff of overtime, the Canucks had constant pressure in the New York zone.
Mike Sillinger also scored for Vancouver, which improved to 4-2-1 in its last seven games.
Marty McInnis scored the lone goal for the Islanders.
In Calgary, Andrei Nazarov and Owen Nolan scored two goals apiece and the San Jose Sharks used a pair of three-goal periods to defeat the Calgary Flames, 6-3.
Cory Stillman, Dave Gagner and Jarome Iginla scored for Calgary.
In Los Angeles, Vladimir Tsyplakov scored twice and 11 teammates recorded points as the Los Angeles Kings snapped a five-game winless streak with a 5-3 defeat of the Hartford Whalers.
Tsyplakov's 12th goal, midway through the first period, snapped a 2-2 contest and gave Los Angeles a lead it wouldn't relinquish.
Geoff Sanderson had his 27th goal for the Whalers.
